Goldman Sachs invests $400M in Cyera, expanding its AI security, data protection and identity management products for enterprises using AI agents

Israeli cybersecurity company Cyera has raised $400 million from Goldman Sachs Alternatives as it works to expand its security products for businesses using artificial intelligence.

The investment comes as companies are adopting AI systems that can access data, use software tools and carry out tasks with less human involvement.

The investment is an extension of Cyera's Series G funding round, which was led by Evolution Equity Partners and announced in June at a valuation of more than $12 billion.

With the latest investment, the Series G round has grown to about $1 billion, while Cyera has raised more than $2.7 billion in total funding. The company plans to use the new capital to develop its products and expand into more markets.

Cyera is expanding its focus as businesses use AI agents for a wider range of tasks. These systems can access company databases, work with different applications and operate using digital identities. Their growing use has created new security concerns, particularly when they are given access to sensitive business information.

Most traditional cybersecurity systems were built around human users and standard software. AI agents work differently because they can interact with several systems and take actions based on instructions. This has increased the need for tools that can show companies what these systems are accessing and what they are doing.

Cyera said the latest funding will help advance its AI Security product roadmap. The company also plans to expand its presence in the US federal market, as well as in Europe, the Middle East and Africa and Asia-Pacific.

"Global 2000 enterprises are telling us the same thing: they need to trust what AI agents can see and do before they can scale them," said Yotam Segev, co-founder and CEO of Cyera . He said the investment would help the company bring its data security and identity security capabilities closer together.

Cyera has developed products such as Agent Guardian and Cyera Endpoint to help companies monitor AI-agent activity. The tools can provide visibility into activities including database queries, tool calls and other actions carried out by AI systems.

The company has also expanded into non-human identity security through its acquisition of Oasis Security. The acquisition adds technology for managing machine and software identities to Cyera's existing data security platform.

By combining these capabilities, Cyera aims to give companies a clearer picture of where sensitive information is stored and which users, machines or AI agents can access it. This is becoming more important as businesses introduce more automated systems into their operations.

Goldman Sachs Alternatives said the growing use of AI agents is creating a new area of demand for enterprise cybersecurity products. The investment will give Cyera additional funding to develop its technology and expand its operations in international markets.

The funding also comes as investors show greater interest in cybersecurity companies working on AI security risks. As businesses increase their use of AI systems, security providers are developing new ways to monitor access to data, manage digital identities and control automated activity.

Cyera is now focusing on the connection between data security, identity management and AI security. The latest funding is expected to support that strategy as the company expands its products and international presence.
